message.content: {"summary":"You produced a balanced, well-supported report recommending not to ship, with strong healthcare and VW/Apple evidence. You did well linking quality-safety tensions to stakeholders and building a logical for/against case. To improve, deepen design and organisational context, tailor guidance to more stakeholders, and add visuals and stronger evidence.","next_steps":["Deepen INTRODUCTION links between ethical issues, engineering design decisions, and organisational pressures to show both context and stakeholder interests.","Extend DICUSSION and The Most Ethical Path to give decision-making guidance for several stakeholders, not just Rachel, including supplier and customer views.","Add 2-3 figures or tables to support discussion and tidy References formatting for consistency and accuracy."],"criteria":{"C1":"You identified several issues in INTRODUCTION, e.g. maintaining product quality safety while trying to succeed as a business, with clear stakeholders. For Excellent, show significance in engineering design and demonstrate both organisational context and stakeholder interests in more depth.","C2":"You gave objective for/against arguments in DICUSSION: To Ship or Not to Ship with a clear not-ship conclusion. For Excellent, add significant depth and give decision-making conclusions for several different stakeholders beyond Rachel.","C3":"Your to-ship/not-ship structure in The Most Ethical Path supports your trade-off conclusion well. For Excellent, develop a systematic understanding for all stakeholders, including chip supplier and health-department perspectives.","C4":"You used four relevant sources in References including NHS HSSIB and Code of Ethics with qualitative and some quantitative evidence. For Excellent, add academic depth with both qualitative and quantitative evidence showing balanced, in-depth understanding.","C5":"You included abstract, introduction, body, conclusion and References with fluent writing. For the next level, use visual elements competently to support discussion and use consistent, well-structured referencing throughout."}}
